title: General mathematics from occurrence and smooth-exponent interleaving
objective: Develop the original smooth-number exponent-stream and occurrence-count observations into a substantive general mathematical result. Explain higher-dimensional behavior with a structural or quantitative theorem and a concrete consequence for fixed-prime ordering or random access. Require a complete uniform proof, reproducible verification, primary prior-art comparison and an honest publication assessment beyond the existing manuscripts. Isolated patterns, known corollaries or a plan alone do not complete the goal.
scope: Fixed-prime smooth-number ordering and exponent streams; general positive-weight mathematics where it explains those observations. No prime-generation, factoring or ML architecture objective.

results: The ordinary occurrence partner of one exponent stream is the rank on the remaining coordinate face; its two-pass return is preserved established background.
For distinct exponent vectors a,b with later rank j, product_i(1+abs(a_i-b_i))<=2(j-1). Their difference therefore involves at most floor(log2(2j-2)) coordinates.
Signs of primitive mixed-sign comparison vectors z with product_i(1+abs(z_i))<=2n determine the full n-term prefix. The argument charges the first rank affected when crossing a comparison wall.

The n-term prefixes on all coordinate faces of dimension at most 1+floor(log2 n) determine the full n-term prefix. This is uniqueness under a joint-realizability promise, not a face-compatibility criterion or a running-time improvement.

For every k and every finite M, two 2k-prime systems can have identical M-term words on all proper faces and differ in the full word by rank binomial(3k,k). The first 2k-1 prime bases can be shared. The prime realization uses established Bertrand-based finite approximation.
The worst-case face dimension required for n-term reconstruction is Theta(log n), uniformly in ambient dimension. Upper and lower leading constants differ; exact thresholds remain open in this study.

A four-prime witness agrees on every proper face through 1000 terms and differs at rank 10. Exact rational lower-bound fixtures in dimensions 2,4,6,8,10 support the general argument without substituting for its proof.

second_iteration.record: docs/occurrence_reconstruction.md, One exponent stream determines the normalized ordering
results: One infinite exponent stream determines every normalized remaining face height by a ratio of placement-rank differences. The indecomposable elements of the recovered additive monoid are exactly the remaining generator weights, so dimension and full ordering are determined up to permutation of unobserved coordinate labels.

The deletion recursion reconstructs the exponent stream from its binary zero mask. The single-mask rigidity is about exact infinite data and does not turn approximate real equality into a finite atom-identification algorithm.

A finite height-error certificate is proved: 8/b+2^m*H*b/a+(2*K+1)*(M(a+K)-M(a))/M(a+1). It uses observable face counts, a dimension bound and a certified coprime rational approximation p/b to one actual remaining generator with error at most 1/b^2. Stream positions, calibration and finite-prefix length are charged rather than assumed free.

For at least three distinct prime bases, normalized recovery plus the classical six exponentials theorem removes the common scale ambiguity and determines the observed prime and all remaining primes. This is an application of an established transcendence theorem, not a new transcendence or prime-distribution estimate. No unconditional two-prime absolute-uniqueness statement is claimed.

For every finite M, two increasing prime triples with the same first two primes can have identical M-term observed first-prime streams but full words first differing at rank 6. The coordinate is active at rank 2. The uniform separating-wall proof and a 20000-entry exact witness delimit the infinite-data theorem.

Explicit finite controls verify placement and clock-increment identities, zero-mask reconstruction, circular endpoints and wrapped intervals, rational lattice counting bounds and rigorous prime-log enclosures. Separate large-clock quadratic-irrational certificates use an exact rank-difference formula checked against direct counts; no huge stream generation or speedup is claimed.

third_iteration.record: docs/occurrence_reconstruction.md, Finite recovery under a quantitative separation promise
results: For normalized remaining weights in a supplied interval [h,H] and a supplied global Diophantine lower bound c/||z||^mu, Theorem 10 reconstructs the first n full exponent vectors from an explicit finite prefix of a single zero mask. Unobserved coordinates are labeled by increasing generator weight.

A Dirichlet argument and the quantitative promise force a sufficiently large approximation denominator without calibrating any unknown generator. The previous finite height bound then applies uniformly at an explicit clock.

All face heights through an integer cutoff covering the generators are observed. Separation distinguishes exact additive decompositions from nonzero forms using rational tests, identifying every generator rather than assuming early face points are atoms.

The observation bound charges every mask bit read, not a placement-rank oracle. For fixed class parameters the sufficient length is O(n^((m+1)(mu+1)^2)); this is polynomial in numerical rank, not its bit length, and constants can be enormous.

The same separation margin preserves all comparisons in the first-n candidate box, giving exact prefix reconstruction with rational weights. Source validity and the global numerical class are unchecked promises, not recognized from finite data.

Fixed prime systems admit some effective promise constants by published linear-form-in-logarithms bounds. This uses established number theory and supplies no new prime-gap bound, finite exact real-weight identification, practical recovery claim or faster unranking kernel.

fourth_iteration.record: docs/occurrence_reconstruction.md, A sharp dimension threshold for finite interleaving
results: A fourth-moment calculation for uniform degree-floor(s/2) weak compositions proves E[Y^4]<=12 E[Y^2]^2 for centered nonzero linear forms; both strict halfspaces have mass at least 1/48. Factorial moments and the moment method are derived and credited as standard tools.

For positive weights with sum at most 2T, at least binomial(s+floor(s/2)-1,floor(s/2))/48 nonnegative integer points lie strictly below height T. The equal-weight, zero-variance case is handled separately. A cyclic-orbit bound improves some finite thresholds.

The minimum first rank of a generic comparison wall involving s coordinates is Theta((3*sqrt(3)/2)^s/sqrt(s)). Balanced full-support walls give matching upper bounds in both parities, arbitrary finite agreement on proper faces and simultaneous prime realizations.

The worst-case face dimension needed for n-term reconstruction is (log n+0.5 log log n)/log(3*sqrt(3)/2)+O(1), for both independent positive weights and actual prime bases, uniformly over ambient dimension. This sharpens the earlier Theta(log n) result to bounded additive error.

The new result concerns labeled coordinate-face prefixes and requires no Diophantine calibration. It does not reduce the number of requested faces, provide a faster unranking kernel or replace the distinct single-mask input assumptions.
